column1:
A company is migrating from an old CRM system to a new cloud-based solution (e.g., integrating sales, marketing, and support modules). 
The development involves integrating many third-party tools (email, calendar, telephony) and migrating historical customer data.

column2: Check if you can find, update, and convert an old customer record to an active sales opportunity without losing data.
Test creating a meeting in the linked external calendar (e.g., Outlook) and verify it appears correctly on the CRM customer record and in the CRM's internal activity log.
Run reports filtering on the oldest date, the largest set of notes, and a non-standard currency from the legacy system. Check for loading delays or data corruption.

Two users simultaneously edit the same high-risk field (e.g., Customer Status or Account Owner) on the same record. Verify the system handles the conflict cleanly (e.g., locks one user out or performs a last-save-wins update).
Log in as a low-level "Marketing User" and attempt to perform high-privilege actions, such as changing the "Sales Owner" field or viewing confidential notes.
Rearrange all widgets, change the color scheme, and apply a complex filter. Save the layout. Log out and immediately log back in. Verify the saved state is loaded instantly and correctly.

Apply a filter (e.g., a specific zip code for regional sales) that you know will return zero data points (a boundary case). Then, apply a filter that returns the maximum possible number of data points. Verify no crashes or rendering errors occur in either scenario.
View the dashboard on a severely restricted screen size (e.g., simulating a mobile phone or a split-screen desktop window). Verify that the layout changes correctly, without data clipping.

Temporarily disconnect one of the underlying real-time data feeds. Verify the charts relying on that feed show a clear, localized "Data Source Disconnected" error, while other charts continue to update normally.

Export the dashboard view (to PDF or CSV) while the data is actively refreshing. Verify the exported file is not corrupted and that the time-stamped data in the file accurately reflects the moment of export, not a delayed state.
